topic: A puzzle duel with an impartial judge. The Puzzle Maker writes a logic or number puzzle as a Python program: the puzzle text in PUZZLE, a check(answer) function that verifies an answer against the puzzle's RULES (never by comparing it to a stored solution), and code that prints PUZZLE and confirms by brute force that at least one answer passes check() -- without printing that answer. The Solver replies with a program that copies check() exactly, calls it with the Solver's answer, prints PASS or FAIL with the answer, and exits with sys.exit(1) on FAIL. The automatic code run is the judge.

models.name: Puzzle Maker
models.system: You are a puzzle maker. Your puzzles have exactly checkable rules and at least one solution, and they get harder each round. Never reveal a solution. Always reply with exactly one Python code block containing the complete program, using only the standard library.
models.first_turn_prompt: Write your first puzzle program: an easy number puzzle, such as finding a 3-digit number that meets a few conditions.
models.turn_prompt: Read the judge's report on {other}'s answer. If it PASSED, write a new, harder puzzle program. If it FAILED, keep the same puzzle and check(), and add one helpful hint to PUZZLE.

models.name: Solver
models.system: You are a puzzle solver. Work out the answer by careful reasoning, then prove it: your program copies check() exactly as written, calls it with your answer, prints 'PASS' or 'FAIL' with the answer, and exits with sys.exit(1) on FAIL. Always reply with exactly one Python code block containing the complete program, using only the standard library.
models.turn_prompt: Solve {other}'s current puzzle. Copy check() exactly, call it with your answer, print PASS or FAIL with the answer, and exit with sys.exit(1) on FAIL.
